success_patterns: The clue's distinctive wording is repeated almost verbatim across many passages with the answer in the blanked slot (mistletoe, Erewhon, Alice Walker, Padre Island). The agent copied that entity as a short bare answer.
Many passage titles ([TLE]) and bodies centre on one entity that also matches the clue's specifics (Charles Evans Hughes, Erewhon, Padre Island). The agent answered with that entity's plain name.

Definition-style clues ('the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line') were solved by finding dictionary passages that repeat the definition and answering with the headword ('homestretch').

When the archived clue was cut off with '...' before the answer (the 51.5 km Olympic event), the agent matched the clue's numeric detail against other passages and answered with the concept they tied to it (triathlon).
For fill-in-the-blank clues ('House Committee on ___ & Infrastructure'), the agent gave only the missing word ('Transportation').

patch.reasoning: All 8 successes shared one workflow: find the clue's distinctive words repeated in the passages, identify the entity or term they converge on, and output it bare. Rules 1-4 already cover verbatim and near-verbatim matching and bare formatting. Three habits are not stated explicitly and are worth reinforcing. (1) Passage titles and the dominant subject across passages point to the answer. (2) A definition clue is solved by matching a dictionary entry and answering with the headword. (3) A truncated archive clue can be completed by matching its numbers against other passages. These help on the failure types seen earlier (refusals and over-long answers) without adding a new top-level section.

edits.target: A phrase repeated across independent passages is strong evidence.
edits.content: - Use passage titles ([TLE]) as a shortcut. When several passages are titled after, or centred on, one entity and also repeat the clue's specifics (dates, numbers, quoted titles), that entity is the answer. Give its plain name ('Erewhon', 'Padre Island', 'Charles Evans Hughes') without extra descriptors.

edits.target: even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - Definition clues ('It's the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line'): find the dictionary or glossary passages that repeat the definition and answer with the defined headword ('Homestretch'), as a single term with no article or definition words. If the clue has a blank ('House Committee on ___ & Infrastructure'), answer with only the blank's word ('Transportation').

edits.target: Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
edits.content: - If the archived clue is cut off ('...') before its answer, match the clue's remaining concrete details (numbers, units, years, quoted titles) against the other passages. Take the concept they all tie to the detail; for example, '51.5 kilometers' appears with 'Olympic distance' passages -> 'Triathlon'. Answer with that concept, not with a nearby number or unrelated page.
